html:
On 10 October 1874 the leading chiefs of Fiji, headed by Cakobau, ceded their islands to Britain at Levuka. Fiji remained a British colony until independence on the same date in 1970.

The first governor, Arthur Gordon, ruled through the chiefs and kept most land in the hands of Fijian clans, where it still is. He set up the Great Council of Chiefs.

To spare Fijians from plantation work, Gordon brought labourers from India from 1879: the start of Indian indenture. A measles epidemic brought back by the chiefs from Sydney had just killed about a third of the Fijian people.
